summary.oneLiner: Precision engineering components manufacturer supplying disc/strip/coil/spiral springs, wedge-lock washers and high tensile fasteners to OEMs and Tier-1 suppliers across renewable energy, industrial and mobility sectors.
summary.business: Gala Precision Engineering Limited designs and manufactures precision engineering components across two business areas: Springs Technology (disc springs, strip springs, coil springs, spiral springs, wedge-lock washers) and Special Fastening Solutions (high tensile fasteners such as studs, anchor bolts, cross bolts, hex bolts and nuts). It serves OEMs, Tier-1 suppliers and channel partners across renewable energy, industrial applications and mobility, with an 800+ SKU portfolio built over 30+ years of operations, 175+ customers and exports to 25+ countries.

currentContext.strengths: Extensive product portfolio of 800+ SKUs built over 30+ years of precision engineering operations|Broad customer base of 175+ customers with exports to 25+ countries|Quality certifications (ISO 9001, ISO 14001, ISO 45001, IATF 16949) supporting customer approvals and audit readiness in safety-critical applications|Diversified exposure across multiple end-industries and a diversified product family (springs and fasteners) cited as the Company's own risk-mitigation approach|Strengthening application engineering capability and deeper OEM relationship management cited as ongoing focus areas
currentContext.strategies: Strategic focus on identifying, executing and successfully implementing key business projects across operating verticals, with funds conserved/retained earnings prioritized for these long-term initiatives over dividend payout.|Continued evaluation of opportunities for future expansion and capacity enhancement, including identification of suitable land for upcoming projects.|Strengthening organizational capabilities through recruitment across middle and senior management levels and creation of new strategic roles.|Move from component supply to application-specific solutions, offering customized springs, fasteners, washers and product combinations for customer-specific applications.|The Board has prioritized conservation of funds and retention of earnings for reinvestment to support long-term business projects and expansion across operating verticals, rather than dividend payout; no dividend was recommended for FY26. The Company maintains a Board-adopted Dividend Distribution Policy (adopted November 30, 2023) under SEBI LODR Regulation 43A.
currentContext.expansion: Capacity expansion is described as continuing through the Company's Wada and Chennai operations, with the Chennai facility oriented toward Special Fastening Solutions. During the year the Company implemented a new 1.8 MW captive solar power project near Nanded, Maharashtra as part of sustainable-operations initiatives, and continued evaluating opportunities for future expansion and capacity enhancement, including identification of suitable land for upcoming projects.
currentContext.mdna: Renewable energy and energy transition (wind, solar, grid infrastructure) seen as relevant demand driver as such applications require reliable load-bearing, vibration-prone and safety-critical mechanical components — disc springs, high tensile fasteners, studs, nuts, bolts and vibration-resistant fastening solutions.|Electrical equipment and power infrastructure (transformers, switchgear, power distribution equipment, circuit breakers, rectifier systems) cited as a relevant application area requiring precision components able to perform under thermal, mechanical and vibration stress.|Railways and metro infrastructure cited as an important application area, with components required to withstand vibration, fatigue and repeated loading in track fastening systems, couplers, traction motors, braking systems and control arms.|Off-highway, construction and mining equipment cited as relevant given high-load, high-vibration, fatigue-prone operating conditions in excavators, loaders, mining equipment, engines, frames and hydraulic systems.|Mobility, commercial vehicles and EVs cited as an application area for fastening and spring solutions addressing vibration, fatigue and thermal cycling, with potential application in battery pack assemblies, braking systems, seating systems, chassis/frame assemblies, powertrain systems and power electronics.|Green hydrogen and electrolyzers flagged as an important emerging application area, with disc springs, studs, nuts, bolts and high tensile fasteners relevant for electrolyzer stack compression frames and end-plate assemblies.

risks.note: IMF's World Economic Outlook (April 2026) flagged downside risks dominating the global outlook, including broader conflict, geopolitical fragmentation, renewed trade tensions, elevated debt and financial market vulnerability — a macro backdrop the Company operates against.
WTO has highlighted that global trade remains exposed to trade policy uncertainty, tariffs, conflict-related disruptions and higher fuel costs, relevant given Gala's export exposure.
Gala's products depend on steel, alloy steel and other engineered materials; sharp movements in raw material prices can affect input costs, working capital and margins.
As a company serving export markets and importing certain inputs or equipment, Gala remains exposed to foreign exchange movement.

risks.risk: Competition from domestic and international players
risks.note: The springs and fasteners industry includes both domestic and global competitors; customers compare suppliers on cost, quality, delivery, technical capability, approvals and track record.
Gala's products are used in applications where failure can affect safety, equipment performance and customer operations, given their safety-critical end uses.

End-user industries such as hydrogen, EVs, railways, renewable energy and electrical equipment are evolving; component requirements may change over a 10-15 year horizon due to new designs, materials, standards and customer expectations.

thesis: Niche precision-components maker (disc springs, coil springs, studs) extending into the much larger high-tensile fastener (bolts/nuts) market via a new Chennai plant, riding wind-energy and industrial-fastener demand to compound revenue ~20-25%/yr with 17-19% EBITDA margins.
scorecard:
| Metric | Q4 FY26 | FY26 | YoY |
|---|---|---|---|
| Revenue | ~INR 95 cr | INR 314 cr | +26% Q / +32% FY |
| EBITDA | ~INR 17 cr | INR 52 cr | +31% Q / +27% FY |
| EBITDA margin | 17.57% | 16.51% | down ~0.6pp FY (forex loss ~1%) |
| PAT | INR 12 cr | INR 36 cr (post-exceptional) | +22% Q / +32% FY |
| PAT margin | 12.9% | 11.29% | — |
| SFS revenue | — | INR 108 cr | +64% FY |
| Inventory days | — | 103 | target -10 days |
guidance:
- Company growth 20-25% revenue CAGR; wind 25-30% short term.
- EBITDA margin to normalize 17-19% by FY27-end (assuming no further forex/commodity volatility).
- Chennai: ~INR 80 cr revenue FY27 (~67-70% of 120 cr capacity); exit run-rate INR 9-10 cr/month.
- Export contribution to stay 35-40% of sales.
- Offshore wind ~10% of fastener sales in 2-3 yrs.
- Cash flow conversion to improve ~10% YoY.
order book / visibility: No consolidated order-book figure given. Price agreements concluded with 4 wind-turbine OEMs for Chennai bolts; commenced high-tensile bolt supply to a global wind OEM in India in Q4; entered offshore wind (Europe global OEM, FY26). Industrial bolt inquiries/orders frozen in gas turbine, railways, mining, construction & agri equipment.
segment:
- **DSS** ~49% FY26 — stable recurring base; includes gallock wedge-lock washers (added ~5 yrs ago, ~INR 1,500 cr global TAM vs ~INR 2,000 cr disc-spring TAM); competes mainly with European producers.
- **SFS** ~34%, +64% FY26, crossed INR 108 cr — fastest grower; studs (~US$1bn TAM) + new bolts/nuts (expands addressable to US$2.5bn global ~US$100bn total fastener market).
- **CSS** ~17% — steady; import-substitution opportunity.
- Margins broadly similar (17-19%) across all three groups.
growth drivers: ~10% new customers/yr + ~10-12% new parts (bolts/gallock/retractor springs) to existing customers + 5-7% organic = ~30% FY26 growth. Fasteners the fastest path on TAM expansion; bolts open industrial verticals (gas turbine, railways, mining, construction, agri).
margins: FY26 EBITDA 16.51% vs ~17.1% FY25; ~1pp / INR 3.23 cr drop entirely a forex (non-cash forward-cover) loss, not mix/RM. RM is 100% pass-through; gas/process cost inflation being passed with a lag (price talks started April). Hedging policy changed: forward cover cut from 70% to 40% of estimated export collections (12-month horizon); US imports give natural hedge.
capex: Chennai fastener plant: 4,600 MT installed; FY26 ~35% utilization, ~INR 5 cr/month (Phase 1 ~INR 60 cr p.a.). Phase 2 underway, complete by Jun-Jul, adds ~INR 60 cr → total INR 120 cr p.a. Phase 2 capex done; SAP S/4HANA + shop-floor IoT rollout; 1.8 MW captive solar ordered. New greenfield: ~INR 50 cr planned FY27 (pending land), capex ratio ~35-40% of incremental turnover.
capital allocation: Funding via internal accruals + bank borrowing. Land: 2-3 own plots in Wada (advanced commercial talks, finalize by Jun/Jul) and SIPCOT long-lease in Chennai. New plant lead time ~15 months (±3). Backup: shift Chennai stud line to long-lease, expand bolt in-house — "will not miss any order."
risks:
- Forex volatility (drove FY26 margin dip); reduced hedge ratio raises exposure.
- Commodity/gas-cost inflation with pass-through lag.
- Patent litigation on wedge-lock washers ongoing (next hearing June; no arguments yet).
- Land/capacity timing — only 1-2 yr runway after Phase 2 unless new land secured.
- Working-capital drag from Chennai ramp-up inventory.
- EU-India FTA benefit (3.7% duty → 0 from Jan-27) likely offset by CBAM.
mgmt tone: Confident and granular; detailed ramp/capacity roadmap; candid that land is "not yet closed" and margin dip is forex-driven, not structural. Constructive on demand visibility.
non-obvious:
- Bolts (not studs) are the real TAM unlock: studs ~US$1bn, bolts/nuts lift addressable to US$2.5bn; industrial bolt pull bigger than studs in many segments.
- Offshore-wind entry (Europe OEM) is a new addressable-market door, targeted ~10% of fastener sales in 2-3 yrs.
- No powder metallurgy — buys sheet/coil/wire/rod.
- Margin dip is non-cash forex, masking stable operating economics.
challenges → beneficiaries & losers:
| Challenge | Direction | Name | NSE | BSE | Role | Conviction | Covered | Note |
|---|---|---|---|---|---|---|---|---|
| Wind/offshore fastener & spring demand | beneficiary | Gala Precision Engineering | GALAPREC | 544244 | Studs/bolts/springs to wind OEMs | High | self | SFS +64%, offshore entry, 4 OEM price pacts |
| Industrial fastener TAM expansion (bolts) | beneficiary | Gala Precision Engineering | GALAPREC | 544244 | New bolts/nuts into gas-turbine/railways/mining | High | self | Chennai 120 cr capacity ramp |
| CSS / coil-spring competition | loser-risk | NHK Spring | | | Japanese coil-spring competitor (Aurangabad/Gurgaon) | Med | external | (code unverified) — foreign listing |
| CSS / coil-spring competition | loser-risk | Stumpp Schuele & Somappa | | | Indian coil-spring competitor (Bangalore) | Med | external | (code unverified) — likely unlisted |
| Disc-spring / wedge-lock | beneficiary | Gala Precision Engineering | GALAPREC | 544244 | Import-substitute vs European producers; gallock | Med | self | Patent suit pending (next hearing June) |
qoq change log:
- Q3 FY26 (call 06-Feb-2026): Chennai generated ~INR 11 cr in Q3; price agreements with 4 wind OEMs concluded; 9M revenue +32%-ish trajectory; SKUs ~750; DSS ~48% / SFS ~35% / CSS ~17%.
- Q4 FY26 (this call): SKUs grew to ~800; Chennai hit ~INR 5 cr/month run-rate, FY26 util ~35%; SFS crossed INR 108 cr (+64% FY); commenced bolt supply to a global wind OEM in India in Q4; entered offshore wind (Europe); Phase 2 capex started (done Jun-Jul → 120 cr p.a.); hedge cover cut 70%→40%; FY26 margin 16.51% (forex-driven dip); SAP S/4HANA + 1.8 MW solar initiated; FY27 Chennai guide ~INR 80 cr; new Wada/Chennai land near finalization with ~INR 50 cr FY27 capex.

themes.title: Commercial-aerospace supply chain (Boeing/Airbus/engine OEMs)
themes.need: A record global commercial-aircraft backlog plus engine-OEM (GE/Safran/Honeywell/RR/P&W) outsourcing and China+1 are pulling Indian build-to-print suppliers up the value chain - aero-engine hot-section airfoils, airframe structures, tooling and wire harnesses. AZAD ramping engine/airfoil exports; UNIMECH near-tripling tooling capacity; AEQUS/SANSERA on precision aero; ROSSTECH on harnesses; PTCIL on titanium castings.
themes.driver: New commercial-aero RFP wins; engine-component capacity ramps; new MRO licences; Boeing/Airbus build-rate recovery.
